seo.title: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Stoke Poges | Fit-Only Installation | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: The bathroom brands we fit in Stoke Poges, and how our fit-only installation model works — your products, our labour, from Duravit and Axor to Victoria + Albert.

h1: Bathroom brands we fit in Stoke Poges

hero.intro: We work on a fit-only basis across Stoke Poges, which means we install the bathroom products you've already chosen — through a showroom, a designer's specification, or your own research — rather than selling you a fixed catalogue of our own. Stoke Poges is a village of large plots and substantial houses, best known for Stoke Park's golf and country club, and the housing stock ranges from older period detached homes to more recent executive-style builds set well back from the road on sizeable gardens. With 30 years' experience fitting bathrooms, we've found that the brands specified in a village like this are often towards the more design-led end of the market, and a recurring set turns up again and again across the projects we take on here — we've built our fitting process around the specific detail each one needs, rather than treating every bathroom brand as interchangeable once it's out of the box.

sections.heading: The fit-only model, explained
sections.body: Fit-only means exactly what it says: the labour and installation expertise, without us also supplying or marking up the products. You choose your sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and fittings through whichever route suits you — a bathroom showroom, an online retailer, a designer's specification, or a brand's own stockist — and we fit them to the standard they're designed for, from a £125 survey through to a finished installation starting from £3,500 fit-only. This works well for a lot of the enquiries we get from Stoke Poges, where a design has often already been through a showroom consultation before we're brought in at survey stage. It also means the quote you get reflects labour and fitting complexity honestly, rather than bundling in a retail margin on the products themselves. Where it matters most is in the detail: a proprietary cistern frame, a volcanic limestone composite bath, or a design-led brassware finish all need to be fitted correctly for that specific product, and we work through exactly what's been specified before a wall closes up or a bath is lowered into position.

sections.heading: Brands we fit
sections.body: Duravit sanitaryware turns up on a good number of the bathrooms we fit in Stoke Poges, usually specified through a showroom alongside SensoWash shower toilet seats or a full ME by Starck suite — the part worth getting right before anything is ordered is the installation route, because Duravit offers its own DuraSystem frame for some pans as well as compatibility with standard concealed cistern frames, and the two aren't interchangeable once a wall is boarded. Villeroy & Boch is another sanitaryware brand we fit regularly, bought through showrooms and retailers across the area — the ceramics are precise and the glaze finishes hard-wearing, but the detail that catches people out is matching flush plate, pan and frame generations correctly, since V&B doesn't manufacture its own carrier frame. For brassware, AXOR is hansgrohe's design-led brand, built around collaborations such as AXOR Starck, AXOR Citterio and AXOR Montreux — the brassware itself is precisely engineered, but the finish is what separates a good installation from an average one, because a brushed or matte black trim shows every scuff mark from a careless fit in a way chrome never does. Dornbracht sits at the top end of the projects we fit, a German brassware house known for sculptural handle and spout design and for finishes that are genuinely difficult to replicate elsewhere; nothing about fitting it is unusual on its own terms, but the margin for error is smaller, since a scuff on a brushed Dark Platinum finish or a rough-in set a few millimetres wrong is far more visible — and far more expensive to put right — than the same mistake on a mainstream brand. Grohe covers a wider span of the work we take on across the village, from thermostatic shower valves and Rapid SL cistern frames through to digital shower and smart water products on more specified projects, and the range is broad enough that we work through exactly what's been chosen at survey rather than treating it as a single fitting job. For baths, Victoria + Albert's freestanding pieces are cast from a volcanic limestone and resin composite rather than acrylic or steel, giving them a solid, cool-to-the-touch surface and genuine weight — a point that matters as much to how we get the bath into a Stoke Poges property as to how it sits once installed, and we plan the floor loading, access route and waste position before the bath leaves the showroom. Kaldewei baths and shower trays, by contrast, are pressed from titanium-enamelled steel rather than cast or moulded, which changes how they're handled and supported on site — the installation detail is about even, accurate bearing across the full base and protecting a hard but chip-sensitive enamel surface from the other trades still working around it.

sections.heading: Why the fitting detail matters more at this specification level
sections.body: At the specification level we see regularly in Stoke Poges, the margin for error on installation detail tends to be smaller, not larger. A scuff on a brushed Dornbracht finish or an inaccurately supported Kaldewei tray is far more visible — and far more expensive to put right — than the same mistake on a standard retail product. That's part of why we work through exactly what's been specified at survey, confirm the installation route for frames, fixings and finishes before any wall or floor is closed up, and sequence the fit so that delicate or design-led products aren't handled more than they need to be. The larger plots and additional space common to Stoke Poges houses often mean more fixtures and a bigger specification in a single room — a double vanity, a freestanding bath alongside a separate wet room — which makes that sequencing matter even more. The product choice is yours; getting it fitted properly, once it's chosen, is ours.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy my bathroom products from you?
faqs.a: No. We work fit-only, which means you choose and supply your own sanitaryware, brassware and tiles — through a showroom, designer or retailer — and we handle the installation to the standard those products need.

faqs.q: Which bathroom brands do you fit most often in Stoke Poges?
faqs.a: Duravit and Villeroy & Boch sanitaryware come up frequently, alongside design-led brassware from AXOR and Dornbracht, and a broader range of Grohe products. We also regularly fit Victoria + Albert and Kaldewei baths.

faqs.q: Can you fit a brand that isn't listed here?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes — we work through the specific installation requirements of whatever's been specified at survey stage. If a product has an unusual fixing or frame requirement, we confirm it before anything is ordered rather than discovering it on fitting day.

faqs.q: Why does the brand of brassware or sanitaryware affect the fitting cost?
faqs.a: Different brands have different fixing systems, frame compatibility and finish sensitivity. A design-led brushed or matte black brassware finish or a composite stone bath, for example, leaves very little room for error on a careless fit, so some products need more careful handling and sequencing than others.

faqs.q: Do you work with Stoke Poges bathroom showrooms and designers?
faqs.a: Yes. A lot of the specification we fit in Stoke Poges has already been through a showroom consultation or designer before we're brought in at survey stage, and we're used to working from an existing specification rather than starting from scratch.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Stoke Poges brands-in-area page, implying brand and material choice through a close fixture detail rather than a full room shot. Subject and action: a close-to-mid shot of a sculptural single-lever basin mixer tap in a matte black finish, mounted above a volcanic limestone composite countertop basin, caught in a still moment with a faint water droplet resting on the tap's spout edge. Setting and work-stage: a finished vanity area in a recent executive-style Stoke Poges house extension, daytime, bright side-angled daylight from an unseen window. Composition: tight three-quarter angle focused on the tap and basin edge, dark honed limestone countertop and a soft-focus sliver of walnut cabinetry visible in the background, tap and basin rim sharply in focus in the foreground. Light and materials: dark honed volcanic limestone composite basin, matte black sculptural brassware, warm walnut veneer cabinet edge just visible out of focus, bright side daylight casting a defined but soft-edged shadow of the tap across the countertop, faint water droplet consistent with recent use. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures, no LED strip lighting anywhere in frame, no twin symmetrical basins, no uniform gold colour wash, no plants, florals or candles as props, no water shown actively running, varied and believable sheen on the limestone with faint realistic water spotting rather than uniform gloss.
image.heroAlt: Close-up of a matte black sculptural basin tap against a dark honed volcanic limestone composite basin in a finished Stoke Poges vanity, bright side daylight with walnut cabinetry visible behind.
